- Overestimate prices in the short term (1-3 days) after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early.
- Underestimate prices after negative sentiment periods; model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17 over 3+ days), model tends to overreact with upward bias; reduce forecast slope.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.22 over 3+ days), model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to compensate.
- Model often overpredicts peak prices in the 10–15 day horizon; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% above recent 7-day high.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 5+ days, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per day.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., +0.17 → -0.22) triggers model lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce magnitude.
- Forecast horizon >20 days: model tends to underestimate true price; add 0.5–1.0% per 5-day interval to compensate.
